svg.title: Unit architecture: who may act, what runs, what moves
svg.text: Unit architecture: who may act, what runs, what moves
Generic pattern generated from a unit spec. Names in ⟨ ⟩ come from the spec; in the filler: ⟨C⟩ = Fill, ⟨P⟩ = NeedleDown, NeedleUp, ⟨E⟩ = NeedleAxis.
① Who may act — unit governance
red: acting state, may run a procedure subapp {…}; Stopping and Clearing end in Stopped
② What runs — skills: each an OPC UA object with Start · Stop · Abort · Reset
internal instances: no OPC UA methods;
loops, choices, parallel branches as pattern FBs
control starts a lane on EXECUTE / STOP / RESET; the lane reports DONE or FAILED
③ What moves — equipment IO CFBs
IO: GPIO · Modbus TCP/RTU · simulator · EtherCAT via a coupler
Inside every skill — primitive or composite
Over OPC UA the same commands are methods with the session ID,
answered at once with [Accepted, ErrorID]; State and Result are published
A Start from the orchestrator is accepted only if
• the skill is not running and its equipment is free
otherwise it is refused at once with an ErrorID
• primitive: holds one equipment command until
Ensures holds; checks Invariant on every sample
• composite: runs its Execute lane; Stop runs the Stop lane
• unit Stop / Abort reach every running skill
IEC 61499 connection or OPC UA call
local channel loc[…]: shared signal, no wiring in the IDE
a typical run: occupy, start the unit, start a skill, it runs its Execute lane,
its primitives drive equipment, the orchestrator reads State and Result
